transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-18
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Marco Alvarez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sofia Park (CTO, ZenHealth AI), Liam O'Connor (Infra Lead), Emma Zhao (Security)
-- Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
ZenHealth exploring Redwood Dedicated for health-data inference. Primary concerns: VPC isolation and encryption, reserved GPU sizing (A100 vs H100-ish), burst capacity for weekly peaks, autoscaling behavior and pricing model (commit vs on-demand). Action: Redwood to send pricing, security docs, and schedule benchmarks.
Topics: reserved GPUs, isolation/VPC and private control plane, burst/scale strategy, benchmark windows, security/compliance checklist.
--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Marco: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Marco here from Redwood. Appreciate you all making time. Quick roll call?
[00:09] Sofia: Hi, Sofia Park from ZenHealth, CTO.
[00:12] Liam: Liam O'Connor, infra lead.
[00:14] Emma: Emma Zhao, security.
[00:16] Priya: Priya Nair, engineering at Redwood, I'm the solutions engineer.
[00:20] Marco: Cool. Agenda — quick discovery to understand your workload, sizing, and constraints; discuss dedicated/reserved capacities and burst options; go over security needs; and agree next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Sofia: Yep, that works. We're on a tight timeline — clinical search and summarization features rolling into a Q3 pilot. Need to know cost and data isolation.
[00:39] Liam: To add, our infra is primarily GCP us-central and we use a VPC with strict egress control. We prefer a private deployment or a VPC-connected dedicated offering.
[00:49] Marco: Understood. Quick qual: current models you run now? Latency targets? Throughput peaks?
[00:55] Sofia: We're currently prototyping with open models — some Llama-family variants and a fine-tuned 7B for summarization. We need 100-200 qps at peak for embedding/short responses and p50 latency under 300ms for small prompts. Production SLOs might relax to p95 < 800ms depending on batching.
[01:18] Priya: Helpful. Do you expect large context lengths or KV-cache heavy workloads?
[01:23] Liam: Summaries usually under 2k tokens, but we plan a clinical record long read where sequences can go 6-8k tokens occasionally, so KV cache size matters.
[01:33] Emma: And data residency — patient PHI must not leave our VPC; we need a private control plane or on-prem routing options. SOC 2 Type II required and possible ISO audit.
[01:45] Marco: Makes sense. So the three big knobs for Redwood Dedicated: reservation size (how many GPUs reserved), isolation mode (dedicated pools in our cloud region + VPC peering or fully private deployment), and burst policy (how we handle spikes — pre-provisioned burst capacity vs best-effort on-demand).
[02:03] Sofia: For reservation, what GPUs do you recommend? We're evaluating cost vs perf. H100 gives big perf but pricey; A100s are cheaper.
[02:14] Priya: Right. For long-context workloads, H100 or those with better memory and FP8 quant ops will reduce token latency. For steady-state embedding-heavy workloads, A100 with optimized kernels and quantized weights can be more cost efficient. We usually model TCO over a month — do you have expected steady qps?
[02:31] Liam: Steady about 40-60 qps, peaks up to 180 during business hours and sometimes 300 for scheduled batch jobs at night.
[02:41] Marco: So a hybrid approach often makes sense: reserve capacity for base load (say enough GPUs to handle 60-80 qps comfortably) and then configure burst pools that can expand for scheduled or ad-hoc peaks. Burst can be internal reserved burst (pre-committed spare GPUs) or on-demand cloud instances — the former gives predictable latency but higher commit; the latter is cheaper but best-effort and may have cold-start latency.
[03:04] Sofia: Latency during peak is critical for clinician workflows. Best-effort burst is risky.
[03:08] Priya: Totally fair. For clinician-facing paths we'd recommend setting a minimum dedicated reserve so fallbacks never hit on-demand. Non-critical batch tasks can use cheaper on-demand.
[03:18] Emma: About isolation: can you describe the VPC options? We need to ensure logs, telemetry, and debugging hooks don't leak PHI outside our network.
[03:27] Marco: Two primary patterns: Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering and private endpoints — control plane still managed but metric/log ingestion happens over direct peered links with encryption in transit. Or Redwood Private where the control plane can be customer-hosted in your VPC/on-prem. For PHI, many customers choose Private or Dedicated with strict egress policies.
[03:47] Liam: How about key management? We must use our KMS and rotate keys.
[03:51] Priya: We integrate with customer KMS (Cloud KMS, AWS KMS, HSM) for at-rest keys. For Private installs, keys never leave your environment. We'll send our KMS integration doc.
[03:59] Sofia: Good. Pricing — are reserved GPUs monthly commitment? Any discount for 12-month?
[04:04] Marco: Yes, reserved is monthly/annual commit; 12-months gives deeper discounts. We can share a tiered price sheet. Important: burst pricing is separate and billed based on usage minute-by-minute for on-demand. For reserved burst (pre-committed spare), it's included in your commit bucket and priced at a different rate.
[04:24] Emma: Auditability — can we get token-level logs for requests and anonymized payloads?
[04:29] Priya: We provide per-request metadata, request hashes, and configurable retention. For PHI, we recommend token-level retention disabled and only store metadata — we can show our log redaction patterns in the security pack.
[04:40] Liam: On autoscaling, how fast can Dedicated scale up? We need short windows to handle sudden daily peak spikes.
[04:45] Marco: For Dedicated with reserved burst, scaling is near-instant since GPUs are already allocated. For on-demand cloud burst, provisioning can take from 60s to several minutes depending on region and instance availability. We also support warm pools to reduce cold starts.
[05:01] Sofia: Tell me more about warm pools.
[05:03] Priya: Warm pools keep instances in a pre-initialized state with model weights partially loaded or cached so start is fast. It's a paid feature; you configure how many GPUs to keep warm.
[05:15] Sofia: For our POC we want predictability and minimal tail latency. I think we'll lean on reserved plus a small warm pool.
[05:23] Marco: Makes sense. Can we talk numbers rough sizing? If one A100 can handle roughly X qps for your 7B tuned model with batching — note X is workload dependent — but for our modelling, assume one A100 ~ 20-30 qps for low-latency single turn generation, H100 could be 1.5-2x.
[05:43] Liam: So to cover steady 60 qps we'd want 3 A100s. For peaks to 300, if we relied fully on on-demand H100, that's a lot. Better to reserve 4-6 GPUs and rely on warm pool burst.
[05:58] Priya: Right — I'll run more precise benchmarks with your model and prompt sets. That benchmark window is key.
[06:05] Sofia: Benchmark plan — we need to run realistic HL7-style documents and our anonymized patient notes set. Can Redwood run the test inside our VPC during the benchmark window?
[06:15] Marco: Yes, for Private or VPC peered Dedicated we can run the workloads inside your network and coordinate the data ingest. We'll need a secure transfer method for the test corpus — scp to a private S3 or a shared GCS bucket with temporary creds.
[06:29] Emma: Also, we need to validate that RTTs between our app and Redwood endpoints meet p50/p95 targets. So we should schedule the benchmark during a time that reflects real traffic.
[06:39] Marco: Agreed. We'll set up a 2-hour window and run steady-state and spike tests. Priya will own the load harness.
[06:47] Priya: I'll draft the test plan and the list of scripts we use. We'll simulate concurrent connections, varying sequence lengths, and cold vs warm cache runs.
[06:57] Sofia: On compliance: SOC2 is required, and we may ask for a custom DPA appendix for patient data.
[07:03] Emma: Yes. And we may request an introduction to your security engineering for a short call.
[07:08] Marco: We'll include our SOC2, ISO docs and a template DPA. Security engineer intro — happy to do that.
[07:14] Sofia: What about model versions and pinning? We need to lock an inference model for the POC. Can Redwood pin model versions across environments?
[07:21] Priya: Yes. Our platform supports model pinning and rollout policies. You can pin to exact model binary or a tag. We'll also support A/B rollouts and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if a pinned model is unavailable.
[07:37] Liam: Does fallback risk exposing data to a different environment?
[07:40] Marco: Fallback follows the same isolation policies; if you're on a private plane, fallbacks occur to other private-compatible variants. We'll include the safe-fallback policy details.
[07:52] Sofia: Ok, timeline — we want a pilot environment by mid-April. Is that feasible?
[07:58] Marco: Yes, feasible. Typical timeline: contract + network setup 1-2 weeks, reserved capacity provisioning 1 week, benchmark + tuning 1 week. So mid-April is doable if contracts start this week.
[08:12] Emma: Procurement and legal will want pricing and DPA asap.
[08:16] Marco: We'll prioritize sending the pricing and DPA template today.
[08:20] Priya: Quick question on observability: can your console give per-route token-level cost and latency breakdowns?
[08:26] Marco: Yes, Redwood Console surfaces per-route model breakdowns, token counts, and cost estimates. We also support tracing hooks.
[08:34] Liam: Any customer refs in healthcare?
[08:36] Marco: We can share anonymized case studies; I'll include a short one about a clinical summarization workload — note: names redacted.
[08:45] Sofia: Any blockers you foresee?
[08:48] Priya: The main blockers are legal around data transfer and KMS alignment. Technically we'll get the network and sizing done during the benchmark.
[08:55] Emma: We need a short security questionnaire filled out. Do you have a standard one?
[08:59] Marco: Yes, we'll attach our security questionnaire + SOC2.
[09:04] Sofia: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[09:06] Marco: Recap: Redwood to send pricing tiers (reserved monthly and 12-month), burst options and warm-pool pricing; security pack (SOC2, DPA template, KMS integration doc); propose benchmark window 2025-03-26; Priya to send test plan; customer to provide test dataset and allowlist. Pilot target mid-April.
[09:25] Liam: That matches our notes.
[09:27] Emma: Fine. Also, please mark any network ports and egress addresses in the network checklist.
[09:33] Marco: Will do. Thanks all.
[09:36] Sofia: Thanks.
--- End of call ---
Notes on transcript: occasional ASR errors: 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', 'H100-ish' shorthand, and some punctuation missing. Links/attachments referenced: pricing_sheet_link (internal), security_pack_link (https://redwood.ai/security-pack/zenhealth), benchmark_plan_draft (to be shared).
